entity_title: Secure a work permit — the entry visa alone will not let you work
fact_text: A foreign professional must hold a work permit issued by a competent Vietnamese authority to work legally in Viet Nam, unless they fall under one of the Article 154 Labour Code exemptions. An entry visa (tourist, business or e-visa) is not by itself authorisation to take up employment.
evidence_quote: Has a work permit issued by an authorized state management agency of Viet Nam, except for cases stipulated in Article 154 of the Code.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work or business visa lets you legally work. Actually you also need a separate work permit (giay phep lao dong) unless an Article 154 exemption applies. Action: confirm your employer has your work permit in hand before your first day.

entity_title: Your employer must justify the hire before your permit can proceed
fact_text: Before a work permit is granted, the employer's application must include a written request explaining the need to hire the foreign worker, on Form No. 03 in the decree's appendix. The process is employer-driven: the labour-need justification comes before the individual's permit.
evidence_quote: Under the new decree, the application dossier must include a written request from the employer explaining the need to hire foreign workers and obtaining work permit, using Form No. 03 in the Appendix attached to the decree.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee drives the work-permit application. Actually the employer must first justify the need to hire a foreigner (Form No. 03). Action: chase your employer to file the demand justification early — your permit cannot proceed without it.

entity_title: Count on a 10-working-day decision once your file is complete
fact_text: Once a valid work-permit dossier is received, the competent authority must decide whether to issue the permit within ten working days. If it is refused, a written explanation must be given within three working days.
evidence_quote: The competent authorities must decide whether to issue the work permit within ten working days from the date of receiving valid dossier.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed work-permit processing is open-ended. Actually the statutory decision window is ten working days from a valid dossier. Action: plan your start date around dossier-complete plus ten working days, not around visa issuance.

entity_title: Apply to the provincial People's Committee, not the labour department
fact_text: Since Decree 219/2025/ND-CP took effect on 7 August 2025, provincial-level People's Committees issue, reissue, extend and revoke work permits. This moved the authority away from the labour ministry and provincial labour departments (DOLISA) that handled permits under the earlier Decree 70/2023.
evidence_quote: The decree assigns the authority to issue, reissue, extend, and revoke work permits to provincial-level People's Committees.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed work permits are handled by the Department of Labour (DOLISA). Actually, from 7 August 2025, the provincial People's Committee is the issuing authority. Action: disregard pre-August-2025 guides that route you to DOLISA.

entity_title: Intra-company transfer is exempt only inside the 11 WTO sectors
fact_text: An intra-corporate transferee is exempt from a work permit only where the move is within one of the 11 service sectors in Viet Nam's WTO Schedule of Specific Commitments and the person has been employed by the foreign parent for at least 12 consecutive months before the transfer.
evidence_quote: Intra-corporate transferees: Temporarily transferring within a foreign enterprise that has established a commercial presence in Viet Nam, within the scope of 11 service sectors under Viet Nam’s Schedule of Specific Commitments in Services to the World Trade Organization, and who have been employed by the foreign enterprise for at least 12 consecutive months prior to the transfer.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any intra-company transfer skips the work permit. Actually the exemption is limited to the 11 committed WTO service sectors and needs 12+ months' prior employment. Action: verify your sector is on the WTO list before relying on the ICT exemption.

entity_title: Assignments under 90 days a year need no work permit
fact_text: A foreign manager, executive, expert or technical worker who works in Viet Nam for a total of less than 90 days in a year (counted 1 January to the last day of the year) is exempt from the work permit. This threshold replaced the older 30-days-per-entry, three-times-a-year rule.
evidence_quote: Entering Viet Nam to work for a total period of less than 90 days in a year, calculated from January 1 to the last day of the year

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the short-stay exemption is 30 days per entry (the old rule). Actually Decree 219/2025 sets it at under 90 days total per calendar year. Action: track cumulative days across all trips in the year, not per entry.

entity_title: Owning at least VND 3 billion of the company exempts you
fact_text: A foreigner who is the owner or a capital contributor of a Vietnamese limited liability company with a contribution of at least VND 3 billion (about US$114,400) is exempt from the work permit requirement (a board member of a joint-stock company with the same stake is likewise exempt).
evidence_quote: owners or capital contributors with at least VND 3 billion (US$114,400) in a limited liability company;

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every foreigner on the payroll needs a work permit. Actually an owner or capital contributor of at least VND 3 billion in an LLC is exempt. Action: if you hold qualifying equity, check the exemption route before applying for a full permit.

entity_title: A work permit lasts at most two years, and your TRC cannot outlast it
fact_text: A granted work permit is valid for no more than two years and may be extended only once, for up to a further two years. Because a temporary residence card is tied to the work permit, its validity is capped by the same ceiling.
evidence_quote: The validity period of a granted work permit must not exceed two years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work permit or residence card can run for five years. Actually the work permit caps at two years with a single two-year extension, and the TRC is bound to it. Action: diarise renewal well before the two-year mark.

entity_title: A temporary residence card ends repeat visa runs and lets you buy a home
fact_text: Foreigners granted a temporary residence card (TRC) can buy an apartment and stay in Viet Nam for the card's full validity without leaving to renew a visa. The TRC replaces repeated visa extensions and eases business and marriage procedures.
evidence_quote: Foreigners who are granted temporary residence cards can buy apartments. They can stay in Viet Nam for a period of time while their temporary residence card is still valid without having to leave the country.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed foreign workers must keep extending a visa and cannot own property. Actually a TRC lets you stay for its full validity without visa runs and buy an apartment. Action: convert to a TRC once your work permit is issued instead of renewing visas.

entity_title: Register your temporary residence with immigration police
fact_text: A foreigner's temporary residence must be declared to the provincial/municipal immigration police under Circular 53/2016/TT-BCA, by logging the residence address and personal and passport details online, with any change updated. In practice the accommodation provider (hotel, landlord or host) files this declaration.
evidence_quote: temporarily-residing foreigners will have to log in the websites of immigration management offices of provincial and municipal police force to provide information on names, addresses, phone numbers, emails of residence sites.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a hotel check-in or a signed lease is enough. Actually your temporary residence must be declared to immigration police (Circular 53/2016), usually by your host or landlord. Action: confirm your landlord or hotel files the temporary-residence declaration to avoid penalties.

entity_title: Get a Level-2 VNeID digital ID once you hold a residence card
fact_text: Foreign nationals holding a valid permanent or temporary residence card can obtain a Level-2 digital identity (VNeID) account. It is used to authenticate for banking and rental agreements, access public services, and store an electronic residence card in the VNeID app.
evidence_quote: Holders of a Level-2 digital identity account can enjoy benefits to authenticate information for banking and rental agreements; access public services more conveniently and store electronic residence cards and other official documents via the VNeID mobile application, available on both Google Play and Apple App Store.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed VNeID is only for Vietnamese citizens. Actually foreigners with a valid residence card can get a Level-2 VNeID account, increasingly required for banking and rentals. Action: register a Level-2 VNeID at an immigration office after your TRC is issued.

entity_title: You must pay into Vietnamese compulsory social insurance
fact_text: A foreign employee who holds a Vietnamese work permit (or practising certificate/licence) and an indefinite- or fixed-term labour contract is a compulsory participant in social insurance. From 2022 the employee contributes 8% of monthly salary to the retirement and survivorship fund.
evidence_quote: Decree 143/2018/ND-CP came into force from December 1 stipulates that any foreign worker working in Viet Nam is a mandatory participant in social insurance if he/she is granted a work permit or practicing certificate or practicing license by a Vietnamese authority and enters into an indefinite-term labor contract or fixed-term labor contract with an employer in Viet Nam.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed foreign staff sit outside Vietnam's social insurance system. Actually work-permit holders on a labour contract must join compulsory social insurance and pay 8% of salary from 2022. Action: budget the 8% employee deduction (the employer adds more) into your net-pay expectations.
